test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The price of sugar rises by 33%. By what percent should a family reduce the consumption of sugar, so as NOT to increase the expenditure?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

 Trick = (Increase% x 100) ÷ (100 + Increase%)

⇒ (33 x 100) ÷ (100 + 33)

⇒ (33 × 100)/(133) = 24.8%

**∴ Required % is 24.8%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method - 1__**Given:

Price of sugar rises = 33%.

Concept used:

​Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

**Calculation:**

Let initial price of sugar = 100

⇒ Initial consumption = 100

⇒ Total expenditure = price x consumption

⇒ 100 x 100 = 10000

Now new price of sugar after increase of 33% = 100 + 33 = 133

But new expenditure is remain same = 10000

⇒ New consumption = expenditure ÷ new price

⇒ New consumption = 10000/133

⇒ % Decrease in consumption = 100 - 10000/133 = 3300/133

**∴ % Decrease in consumption is 24.8.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method - 2__**** ****Given:**

Price of sugar rises = 33%.

**Concept used:**

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Calculation:

Let initial price of sugar = Rs, A

⇒ Initial consumption = B

⇒ Total expenditure = price x consumption

⇒ Total expenditure = A x B = AB

Now new price of sugar after increase of 33% = A x (100 + 33) /100

⇒ 133A/100

⇒ New expenditure is remain same = AB

⇒ New consumption = expenditure ÷ new price

⇒ New consumption = (AB × 100)/(133A) = 100B/133

⇒ Decrease in consumption = B - 100B/133

⇒ 33B/133

⇒ % Decrease in consumption = (33B times 100)/(133 times B) = 24.8

∴ % Decrease in consumption is 24.8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Profit% = [(Selling price - Cost price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Loss% = [(Cost price - Selling price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at loss = Cost price x (100 - loss%)/100

Selling price at discount = Cost price x (100 - discount%)/100
